decisive_items: cervical spine deformity with scoliotic and kyphotic changes
demonstrating scoliotic and kyphotic changes in cervical spine
response.rationale: R2 best matches the dominant clinical presentation of pronounced head and neck flexion (kyphosis) and the imaging finding of kyphotic changes, while R3 emphasizes scoliosis but the primary symptom is flexion. Both share the same raw spans, but R2 aligns more directly with the chief complaint.

rejected.why: No raw support for DISH; only generic flexion and deformity, no bridging ossification or other DISH-specific findings.
Osteoporosis is not supported by raw spans; scoliotic/kyphotic changes are not specific to osteoporosis and no bone density evidence.
Cervical spondylosis is a degenerative condition but raw spans only describe deformity and flexion, no disc or osteophyte findings.
Append-only completion of R2 adds scoliotic changes but does not improve over R2; redundant composite.
Append-only completion of R3 adds kyphotic changes but R3 is less aligned with the primary flexion symptom; redundant composite.
